A1.justification: Both PDFs describe AirQA and EXTRACTOR. Their complete main texts, figures, tables and appendices support reliable comparison, including matching material relocated between sections.

before.justification: Sections 4 and Appendices C–D report original benchmark evaluations, fine-tuning experiments, ablations, a human study and error analyses.

after.justification: V2 retains these empirical results and adds an answer-format compliance check, synthesis-cost measurements and an analysis of fine-tuning improvements.

M1.justification: Both versions retain the explorer–tracker–actor pipeline, rule-based multiple-question synthesis, ReAct actions, five-turn sliding window, final-turn loss masking and error removal. The 19-function evaluation repertoire is unchanged; revised descriptions and usage statistics do not establish a procedural change.

E1.justification: Coverage remains English-language AI papers, four question types and five element categories, with the same ACL2023, ICLR2024 and NeurIPS2024 retrieval scopes. The new diagnostics remain within this coverage. The revised paper count does not establish a new domain or test scenario.

E2.justification: Tables 4–6 retain the same eight QA baselines, backbone models and base-versus-fine-tuned comparisons. The VLM and manual-versus-synthetic training comparisons also remain unchanged. GPT-4.1-mini appears in the new synthesis-cost study, not as an additional competing QA method.

E3.justification: V2 adds sampling protocols for 30 format-check answers and 40 improvement cases, with ten cases per question type. The new cost study uses GPT-4.1-mini and ten-example averages, estimating multiple-document costs by doubling single-document costs. The reported corpus size changes from 13,948 to 13,956; existing training and inference settings are retained or relocated, without evidence of rerunning the main comparisons.

E4.justification: V2 adds answer-format validation in Section 2.2, a 40-case analysis of fine-tuning gains in Appendix D.3, synthesis-efficiency analysis and qualitative human-study feedback. Existing component, scaling, VLM and error analyses remain. The 83% human–LLM agreement check already appeared in v1 Appendix A.3 and is relocated.

E5.justification: Neither version supplies repeated-run or seed counts, confidence intervals or significance tests for the reported comparisons. The new ten-example cost averages specify sample size but do not introduce uncertainty estimation or repeated-run analysis.

E6.justification: Retained performance and error-analysis results are unchanged. New results include 28/30 format-compliant answers, 13/14/13 improvement cases attributed to strategy/behavior/understanding, and estimates of 35 minutes/$0.056 for evaluation and approximately 22 hours/$160 for synthesizing 4,000 examples. Dataset statistics change, including mean question length from 34.84 to 34.52 and objective evaluations from 71.0% to 71.1% in Figure 2.

T1.justification: The task and evaluation definitions, trajectory notation and error-action-rate formula remain equivalent. Neither version adds or revises a theorem, proof, formal assumption or derivation; the new improvement categories are empirical analysis.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction and conclusion retain the same contributions: comprehensive AirQA evaluation and EXTRACTOR synthesis that improves small-model tool use. The 44.14% best benchmark score and the claim that 4,000 trajectories bring a 7B model close to an untrained 14B model are unchanged.

C2.justification: V2 interprets format compliance as evidence of applicability to small models and explains fine-tuning gains through retrieval strategy, tool behavior and understanding in Appendix D.3. Existing coverage, contamination and LLM-judge limitations remain unchanged. The explanation of diminishing 14B gains moves from Appendix D.1 into Section 4.2.

D1.justification: The first-page promise of a future release becomes a statement that code and data are public, accompanied by a repository link. Appendix C.6 adds evaluation and example-synthesis resource estimates and their measurement details. Core hyperparameters, hardware, preprocessing and prompts were already documented in v1.

R1.justification: V2 removes the instruction-tuning references to Dong et al. on data composition, Liu et al. on data selection and Xu et al. on Baize. Its broader positioning remains unchanged. The DeepSeek-R1 publication update and author–year citation format do not introduce new related work.

P1.justification: V2 polishes wording and moves experimental settings, judge-validation discussion and the 14B explanation into the main text. It also relocates ethics information and adds funding and LLM-use statements. These are targeted edits and reorganizations; the main section sequence and narrative remain recognizable.

P2.justification: V2 adds synthesis-cost Table 14 and improvement-analysis Table 17, redraws Figures 2 and 6, and relocates or renumbers retained displays. The conference template changes the title block, headers, typography and pagination, while most figure designs and table structures remain intact.

improvement.justification: V2 modestly strengthens the paper through format validation, a focused analysis of fine-tuning gains, useful resource estimates and concrete code/data access information. Moving important settings and explanations into the main text improves accessibility. The gains are limited: the central method and comparative results remain unchanged, and the small diagnostic studies add no uncertainty estimates.
